source.title: A Systematic Empirical Evaluation of Fixed Adam-SGD Switching for Deep Learning Optimization

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: It compares Adam, SGD, and a fixed Adam-to-SGD switch on held-out benchmark performance, using a different experimental setup from the cited optimizer-generalization studies.
record.gate_note: The tables report test accuracy and minimum test loss by dataset and learning rate. The study does not report training performance alongside test performance, so it cannot establish whether an optimizer has better test performance despite equal or better training performance. M4 is forecasting, outside V4's image-classification and language-benchmark scope.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance of Adam, SGD, and fixed Adam-to-SGD switching on MNIST and CIFAR-10 across five learning rates. These results test V4, including its switching qualification. Ten-epoch comparisons do not establish performance after convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that rankings depend on task and learning rate, Adam is generally consistent, and fixed switching is competitive or superior in selected configurations. Their stronger claims require qualification: MNIST switching has its best accuracy at 0.002 but its lowest reported loss at 0.001, and switching does not improve on Adam across all conditions.
record.recipe_differences: Fixed-switch Adam-to-SGD training compared with Adam and SGD on MNIST and CIFAR-10 for 10 epochs; batch size 128, five listed learning rates, fixed switching ratio 0.8. The paper's tables provide test metrics, not training-versus-test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and learning rate change the relative test accuracy and minimum test loss; the switching strategy also varies in performance across these conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: M4 forecasting optimizer comparisons report task-specific prediction accuracy and test loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer rankings and switching benefits depend on learning rate in time-series forecasting.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science, Volume 3(10s), 2026
record.problems: The study reports no uncertainty estimates or repeated-run variation. It compares test metrics without reporting corresponding training performance, and uses only one architecture per dataset. The paper says results are not aimed at maximal accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: M4 learning-rate results and optimizer comparisons (Table 8, pp. 2065–2066) are excluded because M4 is a forecasting task outside V4's image-classification and language-benchmark conditions. Table 5 and Table 7 loss ranges aggregate across learning rates and do not compare training-versus-test gaps. Table 10's optimizer comparisons are also not extracted because its CIFAR-10 Adam value conflicts with Table 6 and lacks a clearly stated learning rate for each method.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label training and held-out accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, local connectivity, and transferred initialization.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, controlled isolation of decoupled weight decay, and worse held-out performance despite matched or better training performance. Training curves are discussed, but no matched-training-performance generalization comparison is established.
Batch-size comparisons and recipe adaptations for large batches.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other complexity measures.

missing.what: Qualitative training-loss comparisons omitted from the record: on MNIST Adam decreases training loss faster than SGD; on CIFAR-10 SGD retains higher training losses while Adam and switching behave similarly. These results matter because inferior SGD test performance can accompany inferior optimization.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, Figure 2 discussion, p. 2059; Section 4.2, Figure 5 discussion, pp. 2063–2064

record.verdict_notes: States use Adam-versus-SGD disadvantage for ordinary optimizer rows and benefit over continued Adam for switching rows. Numerical values in the rows match Tables 4 and 6. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported. Comparing identical learning rates is not equivalent to independently tuning each optimizer: on MNIST the best listed SGD accuracy is 97.76% versus Adam's 97.65%. The ten-epoch budget and qualitative training-loss evidence limit attribution to generalization rather than optimization speed. Table 10 is already declared excluded; its inconsistent CIFAR-10 Adam accuracy and unspecified method-specific learning rates prevent a clean additional comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Language benchmarks, training-performance comparisons, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD as a targeted recovery comparison.

source_check.notes: Ten-epoch comparisons establish finite-budget rankings, not convergence-matched generalization; no repeated-run uncertainty is reported. Tables 4 and 6 support the checked values, while Table 10, Table 11, and the conclusion contain inconsistent summaries.
